title: Beta-multiplier current-mirror bias cell
topology: A self-biased, supply-insensitive current reference built from two current-mirrored branches: a PMOS current mirror at the top forces equal currents in both branches, while the NMOS half of one branch is scaled by a ratio K (K unit devices in parallel, or a K-times-wider single device) relative to the other, unscaled branch, which has a resistor in series with its source. In equilibrium, the gate-source voltage difference the mirror ratio K creates between the two NMOS devices is forced entirely across that resistor, so the resulting bias current is set by the resistor value and the ratio K rather than by the supply voltage, giving a current (and, via appropriately sized mirror-diode devices elsewhere on the die, a bias voltage or gm) that is far less sensitive to supply variation than a simple resistor-divider bias. Because the all-zero-current state is also a stable equilibrium of this feedback loop, a start-up circuit is required to force the loop out of that degenerate state at power-up.
spec_class: on-chip current/gm reference — supplies bias currents and cascode/tail bias voltages to OTAs, comparators, and other analog PHY building blocks that need a supply- and (to first order) temperature-tolerant bias point without the area/complexity of a full bandgap reference

pdk_portability.notes: The self-biased beta-multiplier topology, the mirror-ratio/resistor equation for the bias current, and the start-up-circuit requirement are fully portable to any bulk CMOS PDK; the resistor's absolute value and temperature coefficient, and the resulting bias current's temperature drift, are sky130-specific and must be re-derived from sky130's specific resistor flavor (e.g. poly, high-resistance poly, or diffusion, each with a different TC in sky130) and MOSFET model temperature coefficients rather than reused from another process's design.

sizing_approach: Choose the mirror ratio K (commonly in the 4x-16x range) as a design trade-off: a larger K gives a bias current less sensitive to the resistor's absolute-value process variation, but requires a correspondingly larger unscaled-branch resistor and more area; derive the bias resistor value from the target bias current and K using the square-law beta-multiplier current relation (bias current inversely proportional to the resistor squared and to a function of K and the process transconductance parameter), then adjust the hand-calculated value in simulation against the actual PDK models, since real (non-square-law) device behavior shifts the achieved current from the hand estimate; size the start-up circuit to inject a small current at power-up sufficient to move the loop off the zero-current state, but design it to turn itself off (drawing no current) once the main loop reaches its intended operating point, so it does not perturb steady-state accuracy; optionally cascode both branches' current mirrors to improve supply rejection of the generated bias current and any bias voltages derived from it.
layout_idioms: both branches' current-mirror transistors matched via common-centroid or interdigitated layout, and built from unit devices repeated K times rather than a single K-times-wider transistor, so the mirror ratio is set by device count rather than by a hard-to-match single wide device

bias resistor laid out as a string of unit resistor elements with dummy elements at both ends to cancel process gradients and edge effects, in whichever resistor flavor gives the lowest temperature coefficient the downstream bias-consuming stage needs
start-up circuit physically isolated, with its brief power-up transient current path routed away from the sensitive core mirror nodes so it does not perturb nearby analog nodes
guard ring around the whole bias cell to isolate it from digital switching noise, since any coupling onto the bias node directly modulates every downstream stage that consumes this reference

source.citation: P. E. Allen and D. R. Holberg, "CMOS Analog Circuit Design," 3rd ed., Oxford University Press, 2011, Ch. 4, "Beta Multiplier Reference Circuit."
source.license_or_openness: Standard graduate-level analog IC design textbook cited here for its topology, sizing methodology, and named ('beta multiplier') terminology only (no figures or text reproduced), per the KB's open-sources-only rule (case 4, textbook-level common knowledge, in kb/SOURCING.md).

notes: Distinct from a bandgap reference: the beta-multiplier cell gives a supply-insensitive current (and, with careful device sizing, a roughly temperature-stable gm bias) but not an absolute, PVT-independent voltage reference the way a bandgap circuit does (compare `sky130-bandgap-reference` in this KB). It is the lighter-weight, smaller-area choice whenever the downstream circuit needs a stable bias current/gm rather than a precision absolute voltage — a very common case for OTA tail currents and comparator bias in area-constrained PHY blocks.
